chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"It does not harm you to move backward behind you if you find tightness in the row, so you move back to the row behind you; and if you are in a row and wish to move forward in front of you, there is no harm in walking towards it."

key_terms.الصَّفِّ: The row of worshippers in congregational prayer
key_terms.لَا بَأْسًا: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to move forward or backward in the prayer row if it is crowded?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the permissibility of adjusting one's position within the prayer rows (saff) to alleviate crowding or seek a preferred spot, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on ease (yusr) in congregational worship. It underscores that the integrity of the row is maintained through continuous alignment rather than rigid immobility, allowing worshippers to move between rows as needed to ensure order and comfort during salat.
